title: The US has now removed two dictators. Putin will be trembling in his boots
snippet: Western leaders must now act swiftly to convert the shock and awe of US firepower into diplomatic leverage over Moscow.

Log in or Subscribe Copy link X Icon twitter Facebook Icon facebook WhatsApp Icon whatsapp email Add us as preferred source Copy link X Icon twitter Facebook Icon facebook WhatsApp Icon whatsapp email The Presidential Standard flies above the Kremlin, indicating that Vladimir Putin is present Credit: Reuters Hamish de Bretton-Gordon Published 08 March 2026 1:16pm GMT Whatever the outcome of the current US assault on Iran, we have already seen a telling strategic outcome: the clerical regime has been decapitated, despite every effort by a powerful nation to protect the late Ayatollah. The psychological ripples of this will be felt in capitals around the world – and not least in the Kremlin, lair of Vladimir Putin.The world has changed: or at any rate the US has. In 2013, Barack Obama said the use of chemical weapons by another dictator, Assad of Syria, was a “red line”. But after Ed Miliband succeeded in killing Parliamentary approval for British action, Washington also backed down.The result was unfettered chemical warfare by Assad against his own people and around 500,000 deaths. I spent a lot of time in Syria over the following 11 years and I can vouch for the horrifying results of the sarin and chlorine attacks. Miliband should be ashamed of himself, but of course he isn’t: he’s still a reliable friend to murderous foreign dictators. I can’t believe that anyone would listen to him given his record, but there you are. Britain is still the same – but the US is not.Washington has acted against Iran on the basis that it may, in time, acquire a nuclear weapon and develop delivery systems capable of reaching the American mainland. Russia already possesses thousands of nuclear warheads, the overwhelming majority of which can reach and are aimed at the United States. That is not conjecture.As I watch from the Middle East, with instability simmering just beyond the horizon, one hears the argument that the United States is expending too much military resource to retain meaningful leverage over Moscow. Such claims betray a fundamental misunderstanding of American military depth. The United States does not run out of air power because it conducts a campaign. And when measured against Russian forces that have bled themselves white in Ukraine, the comparison becomes starker still.Further, it is now evident to all that the qualitative superiority of American and allied air power over Russian systems is profound. The Russian-supplied S-300 batteries fielded by Iran are now twisted wreckage. Indeed, Israel alone was able to suppress the mullahs’ air defences.Moscow’s protection is better, with not only S-400 but supposedly enhanced S-500 systems coming online. But the Russian forces have critical weaknesses – among them the scarcity of the Beriev A-50 radar aircraft, vital for the detection of low-flying threats such as drones and cruise missiles. Russia had only a handful of these in service at the start of the full-scale Ukraine invasion, and has since lost several at the hands of the Ukrainians. It may no longer be possible to maintain a constant airborne watch anywhere. As for the vaunted S-500, another thing which has been shown throughout the Ukraine war is the exaggerated nature of Russia’s claims for its advanced weaponry.One is therefore compelled to consider whether the current strikes against Iran have more than one target. The Iranian theocracy is being struck directly: Vladimir Putin is being struck psychologically. There is, perhaps, a sequencing in Washington’s thinking: Venezuela, then Iran, and ultimately the Kremlin. Moscow cannot be entirely sanguine. The psychological effect of demonstrated force is often more potent than force itself.President Putin has, by most accounts, played for time since the Alaska summit. His strategic objectives in Ukraine have not shifted since the invasion began more than four years ago. If he believed he could manipulate Washington indefinitely, recent events may give him pause.
